narrative.overview:
The interface is a scoreboard in a friendly club hall: flat, square-edged and glanceable, but warm. The structure stays crisp (square corners, 1px lines, no shadows) while colour, letters and small drawn details make it welcoming.

Text is a clean sans-serif; only numbers use the monospaced face so columns line up. Colour is restrained: warm paper and ink, table blue for action and the table, ball orange reserved for stars.
keyCharacteristics: Sharp and flat: square corners, 1px borders, no shadows, no gradients, no emoji.
Warm paper and ink; blue for action, orange only for stars and winners.
Sans-serif for text, monospace for numbers.
Game state shown as data: stars, rank, streak, bars, initials tiles.

rules.name: The Two Accents Rule
rules.body: Table Blue means act or the table. Ball Orange means a star was earned. No third accent hue, except Foul Red for errors.

rules.name: The Column Rule
rules.body: Numbers that belong together share a monospaced column. Names are never set in mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces carry no shadow at rest or on hover.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded into a pill or a card. Warmth comes from colour, letters and small details.

dos: Do keep every control, tab, input and block square-cornered, with 1px borders.
Do use Table Blue for action and the table, and Ball Orange only for stars and the leader.
Do set names and labels in the sans face, and numbers in the monospaced face.
Do show game state as data in the system's own style.
Do size labels to content, keep all text translatable, and place new elements on the 4px step.
Do design for a phone held in one hand.
donts: Don't use emoji, gradients, glows or shadows.
Don't use borders thicker than 1px or round controls into pills.
Don't introduce another accent hue; Foul Red is for errors only.
Don't set Ball Orange as small text.
Don't mix a proportional face into number columns.
Don't place elements by one-off margins or fixed-width text boxes.
Don't add decorative motion beyond the three authored moments.
